#18487. A former professional athlete on selling real estate to other athletes

📅 13 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 3m • 📚 Deep Dive (636 w)

A former professional athlete on selling real estate to other athletes

📅 13 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (636 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Inman

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • While it’s easy to get starstruck when working for an athlete or other high-profile client, Yohann Sangaré, an agent with eXp’s sports and entertainment division, discourages it.
  • Sangaré, a French former professional basketball player who played for 16 years across Europe, sometimes avoids reading up too much about his athlete clients’ accomplishments in their prospective sports so that he can focus on the task at hand: Finding them the right home and advising them on large investments.
  • In a recent development, sangaré came to the U.S.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

While it’s easy to get starstruck when working for an athlete or other high-profile client, Yohann Sangaré, an agent with eXp’s sports and entertainment division, discourages it. “You come as a problem solver, not a fan,” he said.

Sangaré, a French former professional basketball player who played for 16 years across Europe, sometimes avoids reading up too much about his athlete clients’ accomplishments in their prospective sports so that he can focus on the task at hand: Finding them the right home and advising them on large investments.

In a recent development, sangaré came to the U.S. when he was hired to work for Tony Parker, his former teammate, in San Antonio, Texas; he started as a financial advisor for professional athletes. During COVID, he moved into real estate, specializing in finding homes for athletes instead.

Sangaré explains that the pros tend to make a lot of money for a short period of time, and for that reason they’re usually interested in buying investment properties (often right after they’ve found homes for themselves and their family members). A major part of their real estate agents’ job, then, is to keep their eyes on investment properties with the potential for strong returns.

Recent findings suggest that athletes have specific needs. “As a rookie, they’re just starting out, and they may not want to buy,” Sangaré told Taylor Anderson at eXpcon in Salt Lake City last month. Depending on the length of the contract, a rental might be a better idea. “There are times you tell people now’s not the right time to buy. If they feel you’re working in their best interests, they will trust you,” said Sangaré, who is part of eXp’s relatively new sports and entertainment division (which several brokerages offer).

Recent findings suggest that you have to be patient when working with athletes, he remarked, since their situations are tied to ever-changing contracts; of course, players can be traded, and have to move promptly. You also have to be prepared to wait and work with them as they grow in their careers.

What you don’t have to be: A major follower of their particular sports. Sangaré admits that as a European, he doesn’t know much about football or baseball, but that doesn’t stop him from working with athletes in those sports. Sometimes not being starstruck helps him work with a more level head, he said.

But you do need to know the nuances of sports contracts. For example, some leagues, like the NBA, offer several-year guarantees, while others, like the NFL, don’t; housing options will vary based on those.

Often the connection to an athlete client comes through their financial advisor or sports agent, Sangaré remarked. “The sports agent is always talking to the player, and he’ll know to reach out to you when someone gets traded,” he said.

But that can be a long road. Sangaré said it can take anywhere from five months to two years from starting a relationship with a sports agent to seeing any traction with a player, but you want to start that relationship early since once their clients do start to get traded, they’ll undoubtedly be approached by many other real estate agents. One practical tip he gives is going to the NBA Summer League in Las Vegas and taking agents out for coffee or lunch. “You have to be present where they’re present,” he said.

It has been revealed that and when you do get connected to the client, make sure you don’t start with a sales pitch. “You can’t try to sell them something right away,” Sangaré mentioned; instead, you want to counsel them on how they can protect themselves and what they really need to know when buying a home — whether as an investment property or to live in.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Top digital assets like Bitcoin (BTC), XRP, Ethereum (ETH) and Shiba Inu (SHIB) are facing heavy selling pressure following a severe setback in the crypto market after the sudden exit of Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang.

The unexpected exit of the Nvidia co-founder has created pandemonium in the financial world as shares of the artificial intelligence organization have been hit by a heavy sell-off, further straining an already weak crypto market.

It has been revealed that according to reports by Reuters, Nvidia chief executive Jensen Huang resigned on Nov. 12. Chief Financial Officer Colette Kress has taken over as interim chief executive.

There are controversies surrounding Huang's personal life and doubts about his future at the tech giant he co-founded over three decades ago.

The news of Huang's exit has triggered a heavy sell-off in Nvidia stock, with shares dropping over 12% in early trading, wiping out an estimated $500 billion in market value.

The sell-off has also affected crypto-related trading markets.

As recently revealed by blockchain analytics platform Lookonchain, a trader known as 0x7368 had his leveraged long position in Nvidia stock fully liquidated.

According to Lookonchain, the trader had 9,959 units of Nvidia (NVDA), worth about $1.54 million, liquidated after news of Jensen Huang's resignation hit the market.

Meanwhile, the crypto market itself is reeling from heavy losses as some top altcoins are faring worse than Bitcoin.

The recent crypto market data demonstrates that Bitcoin (BTC) is currently trading around $71,323, shedding about 3% in the last 24 hours.

Over the last seven days, the largest cryptocurrency by market cap has lost even more, shedding about 10.2%.

However, XRP has seen a more pronounced sell-off.

The Ripple-linked cryptocurrency currently trades at about $1.02 after losing 3.3% in the last 24 hours.

The launch builds on the BoomerangFX team's experience delivering more than 10,000 Google, Meta and Instagram campaigns over the past decade. Its proprietary machine learning and data science models combine that marketing experience with specialty context and performance analysis to inform campaign development and optimization.

Sources indicate that AUVIAâ¢'s specialty knowledge framework spans in excess of 2,000 specialty treatment and clinical-indication entries, covering procedural nomenclature, treatment modalities and concerns such as cutaneous photodamage, dermal laxity and dyspigmentation. This context supports relevant patient communication, while clinical assessment and treatment selection remain with the practitioner.

Leadership in Aesthetics Innovation and Clinical Education.

Clinical guidance is informed by BoomerangFX's medical advisory board, led by Dr. Stephen Mulholland, Co-Founder and Chief Clinical Architect of BoomerangFX. A globally recognized cosmetic surgeon, Dr. Mulholland is a co-founder of InMode, where he helped lead its 2019 NASDAQ IPO, co-creator of Morpheus8 and co-developer of BodyTite, FaceTite and AccuTite.

"Aesthetic and wellness practices need technology that understands the language of their specialties and the expectations of their patients," mentioned Dr. Stephen Mulholland, Co-Founder and Chief Clinical Architect of BoomerangFX. "Connecting specialty-level marketing with responsive communication and a complete clinical record helps practices deliver a more consistent experience from the first question through continuing care.".

Availability: Rollout Beginning November 2026.

Upgrade pathways are available for existing BoomerangFX RUN and GROW clients. The launch extends BoomerangFX's recurring subscription platform across patient acquisition, AI engagement, clinical software and payments.

ChatGPT ad activation depends on market availability, practice specialty and advertiser approval. Search Optimization Intelligence supports organic discoverability on Claude and Gemini; inclusion, rankings and recommendations remain determined by each platform. Paid placements are separate from AI-generated answers.

BoomerangFX operates in a growing list of international markets, including the USA, Canada, the UK, Ireland, Germany, Australia, India and Latin America. With offices in Miami, Toronto, London and Sydney, BoomerangFX is advancing its mission to become the foundational operating platform for private-pay healthcare worldwide.

It has been revealed that ELEVATE is BoomerangFX's premium specialty healthcare marketing solution, with campaign experience in more than seven countries across medspas, cosmetic surgery, hair restoration, women's health, weight management, longevity and functional medicine. Its international resources span strategy, branding, website design, paid advertising, SEO, social media, content, campaign optimization and performance reporting.

Alibaba releases Qwen4-Max with training, attention optimizations

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that alibaba Group Holding Ltd.
  • According to recent reports, the algorithm not only generates higher-quality output than its predecessor but also costs less.
  • Sources indicate that qwen4-Max’s backbone, the part of an LLM that functions as its main processing engine, comprises 2.4 trillion parameters.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

UPDATED 16:21 EST / NOVEMBER 16 2026.

It has been revealed that alibaba Group Holding Ltd. today introduced Qwen4-Max, its newest and most capable large language model.

According to recent reports, the algorithm not only generates higher-quality output than its predecessor but also costs less. Those improvements are the result of a fresh architecture, Qwen4, that made the LLM’s training run more efficient. Additionally, Alibaba has equipped the model with an upgraded attention mechanism.

Sources indicate that qwen4-Max’s backbone, the part of an LLM that functions as its main processing engine, comprises 2.4 trillion parameters. The model activates only 71 billion at any given time. The backbone is supported by 328 billion so-called N-gram parameters, which function as a kind of cache. They save the results of oft-repeated calculations and thereby remove the need to compute them from scratch every time.

According to recent reports, an LLM’s artificial neurons are organized into sets known as layers. When the model learns something fresh during training, a piece of data called a gradient travels through the layers and refines their output. The gradient moves through them one by one starting from the last layer, which finalizes and displays prompt responses.

In a recent development, qwen4-Max includes a feature that enables the gradient to skip some layers. That feature, or residual, is effectively a shortcut inside the LLM. Its purpose is to reduce errors during the training workflow, which in turn lowers costs and improves output quality.

In a recent development, residuals can also be found in many other LLMs. Historically, the mechanism was implemented as a single gradient transportation channel. Qwen4-Max’s implementation of the technology features four channels. Moreover, those channels have a “gate” that can adjust the movement of gradients to further improve the training process.

Qwen4-Max’s attention mechanism, a module that helps it understand user prompts, features two key customizations. The first is a technology called Gated DeltaNet that lowers the amount of hardware needed to process large prompts. The second optimization, QSA, skips pieces of data that the LLM doesn’t need to answer a prompt. That arrangement further lowers infrastructure costs.

In a recent development, alibaba compared Qwen4-Max with its predecessor, Qwen3.8-Max, using an internal benchmark that includes knowledge work tasks. The former model achieved a higher score and used up to 35% fewer tokens to complete tasks. Those savings grew to 49% when the models were tested using the Terminal-Bench 4.0 suite of coding challenges.

Qwen4-Max is available through Alibaba’s cloud platform. The company prepares to open-source a collection of smaller models based on the same technologies further down the line. It’s also open-sourcing Qwen-Live-Delivery-Plugin, an extension that makes Qwen4-Max better at performing time-consuming tasks.

When an LLM is assigned a long-horizon project, customers often have to wait until the model completes its work before they can review the results. Alibaba’s plugin shortens the wait. It enables Qwen4-Max to promptly deliver an initial draft and then iteratively add improvements. Users can give the model feedback along the way to refine its work.

Latest Update: Sometimes the most valuable data is the house nobody bought

📅 13 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (819 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Inman

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Canceled listing data in the MLS can reveal where buyers noted no.
  • When agents sit down to price a listing, we know the drill: Pull the solds.
  • But there’s another category of data sitting right there in the MLS that we frequently overlook: the houses nobody bought.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Want to price more precisely? Canceled listing data in the MLS can reveal where buyers noted no. Learn three steps to add failed listings to your next CMA.

When agents sit down to price a listing, we know the drill: Pull the solds. Look at what’s coming soon, active and pending. Adjust for condition, location, square footage and amenities. Figure out where our house fits.

But there’s another category of data sitting right there in the MLS that we frequently overlook: the houses nobody bought.

Expired. Canceled. Withdrawn. Earlier in my career, I looked at these failed listings all the time. Then the market changed. When inventory became tight, and buyers were competing for homes, digging through failed listings often wasn’t necessary to determine where a property would sell.

Now the market is shifting again; pricing must be more precise, and I’m sharpening my approach by bringing an old tool back into my pricing process.

A sold comp tells us where a buyer stated yes, but a failed listing can help us figure out where buyers said no. And in a buyer-favored market, that’s valuable information.

Industry observers note that imagine you’re pricing a home, and the recent comparable sales range from $600,000 to $625,000. Then you expand your search.

Suddenly, you know considerably more than the sold comps alone told you. Other sellers have already tested the upper limits of pricing, and buyers responded. It’s essentially a series of pricing experiments someone else conducted for you — and they paid the carrying costs.

It has been revealed that one of the most interesting things buried in MLS history is the pricing journey. A property might show a final list price of $649,000 and an eventual sale of $630,000. Dig deeper, and you may discover this:.

$725,000 → $699,000 → $675,000 → canceled → relisted at $649,000 → sold for $630,000.

That’s a different story. The sale tells us what one buyer eventually paid. The listing history tells us buyers had previously rejected that house at $725,000, $699,000 and $675,000.

It also illustrates something sellers don’t always understand: Getting to the right price eventually isn’t necessarily the same as pricing correctly from the beginning. After months of market exposure and multiple reductions, buyers may stop asking, “Could this be the house?” They start asking, “What’s wrong with it?”.

In a recent development, when I find a comparable property that sat for 90 days without selling, I want to know what did sell during those same 90 days. Sometimes we blame the market when the market was functioning just fine. Buyers were buying houses. They simply weren’t buying that one.

Maybe they chose the renovated house at $640,000. Maybe they paid $650,000 for the better lot. They may have even paid more for another property because it offered something the failed listing didn’t. That’s useful information when you’re sitting across from a seller who believes buyers just need more time to appreciate their home.

If buyers repeatedly toured the property and purchased competing homes instead, the market may already have delivered its opinion.

Sources indicate that this is where agents have to resist oversimplifying the data. An expired listing isn’t automatic proof that a house was overpriced, and a canceled listing certainly isn’t either.

Recent findings suggest that listings fail for all sorts of reasons. Sellers change their minds. Job transfers fall through. Repairs surface. Agents get fired. Sometimes a seller receives a perfectly acceptable offer and decides not to move.

So, investigate. Call the previous agent. I might simply say:.

“I’m pricing a similar property and noticed yours was on the market last year. Is there anything you can tell me about the activity or why the seller decided not to continue?”.

Twenty-seven showings and no offers tell me something. Two showings in four months tells me something different.

There’s one more number worth considering: the cost of the pricing journey.

Recent findings suggest that find a house that started high, sat, reduced, expired, relisted and eventually sold. Then compare it with similar homes that entered the market closer to where buyers were actually buying.

Industry observers note that sellers often view aspirational pricing as a no-risk strategy: “We can always come down.” Technically, that’s true. But time isn’t free, and neither is market perception.

The next time you’re preparing a CMA in a shifting or buyer-favored market:.

In a recent development, we’re very good at studying success in real estate. But as pricing gets harder, I’ve found myself returning to an old habit: studying the failures, too. Sold listings tell us where buyers have been willing to say yes. Sometimes the house nobody bought is the one that tells us exactly where they started saying no.

It has been revealed that roxanne Hale is the associate broker of the Art House Team, brokered by RealtySouth in Birmingham, Alabama. Get connected on Facebook or YouTube.

Yoshitaka Kitao, head of Japanese financial group SBI Holdings, answered "YES" when asked point-blank whether he still trusts XRP.

The question came from an X user. The user wrote that the past few weeks had been "truly exhausting" for XRP holders, and said that token holders feel that Ripple has left them behind.

Kitao answered in English. Most of his recent posts on X are in Japanese, and the rest of them are reposts of other accounts.

In a recent development, kitao previously worked as an executive at Nomura Securities and later served as CFO of SoftBank. In 1999, he founded SoftBank Investment, which later became SBI Holdings. Today, SBI includes banks, brokerage, and insurance businesses, as well as crypto services.

According to recent reports, the partnership began in 2016. SBI joined Ripple's Series B round and launched a joint venture with Ripple, SBI Ripple Asia. SBI owns about 60% of the venture, and Ripple owns the remaining 40%.

The same year, SBI Ripple Asia set up a consortium of Japanese banks to test Ripple's technology for payments, and the consortium later grew to more than 60 banks.

In 2018, SBI rolled out the interbank app MoneyTap. The same year, SBI's crypto exchange, now called SBI VC Trade, started operations with XRP trading. In 2019, Kitao joined Ripple's board of directors.

From 2020, SBI began handing the token out to shareholders as bonuses, and the payment service SBI Remit debuted remittances using it with on-demand liquidity (ODL), including in the major Japan-Philippines corridor.

SBI kept working with Ripple during the SEC lawsuit against the manufacturer, which lasted from December 2020 until 2025.

Industry observers note that back on February 15, 2026, in rare long-form tweets in English, Kitao denied rumors that SBI holds $10 billion worth of XRP: "Not $10 billion in XRP, but around 9% of Ripple Labs. So our hidden asset could be much bigger." By his account, the combined valuation of Ripple Labs and its ecosystem is "enormous," and SBI owns more than 9% of all of it.

Kitao also talked about XRP at SBI's quarterly briefing on November 2, 2026. He remarked that investors buy Bitcoin mostly to hold it, and that the value of XRP depends on its use in payments and business ecosystems.

In August 2025, SBI VC Trade and Ripple agreed to bring the RLUSD stablecoin to Japan. In October 2025, SBI also invested $200 million in Evernorth, a company that holds XRP in its treasury. By now, SBI VC Trade has more than two million accounts.

At press time, XRP is trading at $1.02.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • In a recent development, the “First Responders’ Time to Own” program gives state and local police officers, full-time and volunteer firefighters and emergency medical service personnel $25,000 in forgivable assistance through the Connecticut Housing Finance Authority (CHFA) and the Connecticut Department of Housing.
  • In addition to down payment and closing cost help, the program gives applicants a 0.125 percentage point interest rate reduction on their CHFA first mortgage.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Connecticut is the latest state to help first responders reach their homeownership goals with assistance for down payments and closing costs.

In a recent development, the “First Responders’ Time to Own” program gives state and local police officers, full-time and volunteer firefighters and emergency medical service personnel $25,000 in forgivable assistance through the Connecticut Housing Finance Authority (CHFA) and the Connecticut Department of Housing. To qualify, first responders must have completed two years of service and purchase a primary residence within the community they serve.

In addition to down payment and closing cost help, the program gives applicants a 0.125 percentage point interest rate reduction on their CHFA first mortgage.

Recent findings suggest that “Connecticut’s police officers, firefighters and EMS personnel dedicate themselves to protecting our families and communities, and we want to make sure they have the opportunity to build their own futures here,” Governor Ned Lamont remarked in a prepared statement on Tuesday. “By helping reduce one of the biggest barriers to buying a home, we’re investing in the people who serve our state and the communities that depend on them.”.

The program is part of Public Act 26-12, a state bill that aims to increase the number of first responders with a number of incentives, including college tuition reimbursement and improved labor protections.

“The people who protect and serve our communities should be able to afford to live in those communities, and this program with help them do it,” Comptroller Sean Scanlon mentioned in a written statement. “Helping the people who put their lives on the line for us every day buy their first home is literally the least we can do, and I’m proud to have worked with Governor Lamont and legislature to make this a reality.”.

It has been revealed that seven other states also have down payment assistance programs for first responders. Florida, Nevada, Georgia and South Carolina provide flat amounts, ranging from $10,000 to $35,000. Texas, Maryland and Ohio’s programs are percentage-based and offer assistance ranging from 2.5 percent to 5 percent of the purchase price.

It has been revealed that the terms of each program vary. Most states forgive the assistance after five to seven years, but Nevada requires homebuyers to repay the funds within 30 years. And like Connecticut, Ohio also offers a 0.25 percent mortgage rate discount.

“Homeownership offers more than a place to live. It creates stability, strengthens connections to community and provides an opportunity to build wealth over time,” CHFA CEO and Executive Director Nandini Natarajan said in an announcement. “Through First Responders’ Time to Own, we’re helping the people who answer the call for our communities take an crucial step toward achieving their own homeownership goals.”.

First responders often fall through the cracks of housing assistance programs because they don’t earn enough to afford market-rate housing but earn too much to qualify for federal housing vouchers.

According to recent reports, inman explored this dilemma last September in a feature on workforce housing in resort towns like Jackson Hole, Vail and Tahoe. These towns can’t operate without first responders and other essential workers in the hospitality and retail sectors. However, rental and for-sale home prices have far outpaced what these workers earn, forcing them to commute long distances from more affordable towns or take on second and third jobs to survive.

The solution for some of these towns has been investing in workforce housing, which caps prices for households that earn between 60 percent and 120 percent of their area’s AMI. Most workforce housing is rent-only, but some states are extending the programs to include for-sale properties.

Recent findings suggest that “I think the fact that workforce housing can be necessary or is a thing in the first place is really an indictment of the state of housing affordability in the country today,” Realtor.com Senior Economist Jake Krimmel said. “I think it’s vital to ground any conversation about workforce and affordable housing in that reality. It’s a market failure and a policy failure that someone could be a doctor, a teacher or another kind of professional and cannot afford to pay the market rent or own a home outright.”.

Windermere Principal Economist Jeff Tucker stated workforce housing isn’t a panacea for affordability and works within an ecosystem of other housing and economic policies, such as upzoning, to create a more equitable market.

Industry observers note that tucker’s comments came a month after the Senate introduced the ROAD to Housing Act of 2025, and three months before the House introduced the Housing for the 21st Century Act. The bills were eventually combined into the 21st Century ROAD to Housing Act, which passed in June.

It has been revealed that “A broad package of necessary reforms to make more housing construction possible in much of the country is a really key component of a long-term solution to the housing affordability challenges we face,” Tucker stated. “Our current housing shortage took years to develop. So it’ll take years to build our way out of it.”.

"The result is a revolutionary capability for commercial and government applications operating at the fundamental quantum limit of sensitivity.".

To bring this vision to light, Weinstein built a team at GenQ that merges theoretical quantum physics with a pragmatic engineering mindset, resulting in quantum solutions that can be readily deployed across private and public sectors. 📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

UPDATED 18:45 EST / NOVEMBER 16 2026.

Noeri Inc., a startup developing artificial intelligence systems that continuously improve their outputs as they learn from an organization’s data and work, is launching with $110 million in funding.

Recent findings suggest that today’s round was led by Menlo Ventures and saw participation from Seattle-based Madrona Ventures, Kindred Ventures, Wing Venture Capital and NEA. Snowflake and Cisco Ventures also took part in the round.

Noeri is the brainchild of Yejin Choi (pictured, left) and Carlos Guestrin (right), two prominent AI researchers from Stanford University, who spent years developing self-improving systems at the University of Washington prior to moving. The startup’s software is designed to study a organization’s data, workflows and business processes.

Then as it learns about them, it will begin to propose changes regarding specific tasks, in order to make them more efficient. The co-founders refer to it as a “living” AI system that gets better at what it does over time.

For instance, it might offer different instructions, suggest different tools or switch out the model that handles each step of a workflow for another. Each of these suggestions comes with an explanation and is sent to a human for review before it’s accepted, similar to how AI-generated code changes are implemented.

Noeri is compatible with both open-weight and proprietary AI models and ensures that customers retain full ownership of their workflows and the AI systems they develop. Choi told Bloomberg in an interview that Noeri is trying to appeal to organizations that find themselves having to choose between either paying fees they can’t afford for the most capable AI models, or else accepting results from a less effective one.

In a recent development, the idea for the company stemmed from an effort to help a microbiology and immunology team at Stanford use OpenAI Group PBC’s models in a more cost effective way. According to Choi, she and Guestrin developed a small AI model that learned how to use OpenAI’s older models, and to their surprise, managed to fine-tune it to perform better than the more advanced GPT-5 on that research team’s projects.

Industry observers note that the startup’s name was carefully chosen. Noeri means “intelligence, in the plural,” and it’s meant to reflect Choi’s and Guestrin’s belief that the future of AI won’t be dominated by just one or a handful of extremely powerful AI models.

Sources indicate that guestrin especially is a big proponent of choice in the AI industry. In a speech at Madrona Ventures’ IA40 Summit in September, he notably argued that the future of intelligence cannot be controlled by just one or two companies that own the models.

“Few companies would build their core operations on a single consultant who also advises every competitor, can change its terms at will and can never be brought in-house,” Choi and Guestrin wrote in a blog post outlining the startup’s mission. “A single, centralized AI offers exactly that arrangement.”.

Industry observers note that noeri isn’t the only proponent of such a multimodel future. Similar arguments have been made by Mira Murati’s Thinking Machines Labs Inc., which last year debuted Tinker, a cloud-based service that anyone can use to fine-tune AI models and enhance their performance. Similarly, Applied Compute Inc. embeds engineers with its customers to help them fine-tune AI systems.

Industry observers note that guestrin previously helped develop a popular machine learning tool called XGBoost, which is used by researchers to boost the performance of AI models. He also co-founded an early machine learning startup GraphLab Inc., later known as Turi Inc., which was acquired by Apple Inc. in 2016. After that, he joined Apple too and went on to lead that firm’s machine learning and AI research organization.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Ripple's US dollar-backed stablecoin RLUSD has set a fresh record by surpassing PayPal USD (PYUSD) in market capitalization to cement its position as a top stablecoin globally.

Recent data from CoinGecko shows that RLUSD's market cap has grown to around $2.71 billion, enabling it to surpass its competitor, PayPal's stablecoin, with a market cap of around $2.69 billion.

This milestone was achieved less than two years after Ripple's formal introduction of RLUSD in December 2024, underscoring its rapid growth in the crypto market.

A prominent XRP Ledger validator, Vet, also commented on this development to underscore the increasing significance of RLUSD in the stablecoin industry.

In a recent development, "RLUSD is now a Top 5 USD backed stablecoin. On its way to be in Top 3," Vet commented.

Sources indicate that vet noted Ripple's long-standing contribution to building the XRP Ledger. He added that the increasing adoption of RLUSD could potentially lead to faster adoption of the blockchain by traditional financial institutions.

Vet stressed the increasing relevance of RLUSD's rising payment volume and increased use of the stablecoin on the XRP Ledger.

He also noted that RLUSD has opened the door to numerous integrations with banks and crypto exchanges.

The XRP Ledger validator further noted that these integrations could motivate financial institutions to not only run infrastructure to support the XRPL but also integrate other tokenized assets on it.

This new record for RLUSD comes on the back of several key institutional partnerships and exchange integrations for RLUSD that Ripple has been announcing recently.

On Oct. 28, Ripple declared a partnership with Coinbase to provide RLUSD for retail and institutional users across Coinbase Exchange, Coinbase Prime and its retail trading app.

As part of the partnership, Coinbase also declared support for RLUSD across different blockchain networks such as the XRP Ledger, Ethereum and Base.

On the other hand, Ripple's partnership with banking giant BNY, which is the custodian of reserves for RLUSD, is also deepening.

Besides this, Ripple has also managed to secure support from Standard Chartered, which debuted institutional custody services for RLUSD on the XRP Ledger back in October.

Not only is Alex Vidal the new president of REMAX, but the company has clarified that his appointment to this position also encompasses REMAX Canada, making him the leader of REMAX’s Canadian operation.

Vidal was named president of REMAX in September, after The Real Brokerage completed its acquisition of REMAX, forming the Real REMAX Group.

In an emailed statement, a REMAX spokesperson told HousingWire that the president of REMAX has always overseen the manufacturer’s Canadian operation.

As Vidal moves into the Canadian leadership position, Don Kottick, who has served as the president of REMAX Canada since April 2025, has announced plans to leave the firm on Dec. 15. This information was conveyed to REMAX brokers and franchisees via an internal memo reviewed and confirmed by HousingWire.

“This move helps ensure every REMAX region around the world receives as much of the same focus, momentum and opportunities as possible,” the internal memo stated. “The next few months will be pivotal as we roll out new technology and invest in further strengthening the REMAX brand in Canada and around the world.”.

Prior to joining REMAX, Kottick was the president and CEO of Sotheby’s International Realty Canada.

In a recent development, before joining REMAX, Vidal served as the president of ERA Real Estate, helping lead the brand through Compass International Holdings’s acquisition of its parent firm Anywhere Real Estate. Compass and ERA are at the moment suing Vidal, claiming that he violated non-compete agreements through his move to REMAX. In the legal complaint filed in mid-October, Compass claims that the non-compete agreement prevents Vidal from serving as president or providing service to any competing business for a period of one year from his departure from ERA.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Billionaire and longtime Bitcoin (BTC) supporter Tim Draper predicts a future where Bitcoin absorbs the innovations of other altcoins.

Draper's statement has major implications for major cryptocurrencies like XRP, Ethereum (ETH) and Dogecoin (DOGE), which have built their own ecosystems and now compete in the wider cryptocurrency market.

In a recent post on X, Draper compared Bitcoin's rising dominance to Microsoft's path to becoming the dominant software company, as the company absorbed successful innovations from other businesses.

According to recent reports, "Microsoft never invented the spreadsheet, word processor, or slide deck. They absorbed them," stated Draper.

The billionaire investor brought up pioneering software like Lotus 1-2-3 and WordPerfect, which eventually saw their dominance give way to Microsoft's Excel and Word.

Draper predicts that this could apply to the cryptocurrency industry, as Bitcoin could become the ultimate absorber of innovations from alternative blockchain networks.

"Altcoins are the Lotus 1-2-3s and WordPerfects of this time," wrote Draper.

Smaller cryptocurrencies are thus essentially incubators for technological innovations that could eventually become part of the bigger Bitcoin ecosystem, according to Draper.

"They show that it works, then the innovation that pulls the strongest gets ported to the Bitcoin platform," he added.

Draper also supported his statement by citing the rising market share of Bitcoin in the overall cryptocurrency market.

The billionaire investor recalled observing how Bitcoin dominance rose from about 40% to 50% and then even further to 61%.

"Bitcoin is that platform," mentioned Draper, claiming that the biggest cryptocurrency could follow a path similar to Microsoft's.

This statement has implications for the future of major altcoins like Ethereum, XRP and Dogecoin.

Ethereum is the leading smart contract and dApp platform, while XRP is mainly known for its cross-border payments and the wider XRP Ledger ecosystem. Meanwhile, Dogecoin is one of the most iconic meme coins in the cryptocurrency market.

Still, the growing ecosystem around Bitcoin, which adds more scaling and programmability through solutions such as the Lightning Network and projects like Stacks, shows how Bitcoin is trying to expand beyond its basic use case as a cryptocurrency.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Industry observers note that founded in 2019, Villa says it has delivered more than 425 homes using an offsite construction model that spans accessory dwelling units (ADUs), multifamily projects and newly introduced neighborhoods.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Villa, a San Francisco-based manufactured homebuilder, has appointed homebuilding and real estate veteran David Messenger as CEO, the tech giant announced on Monday.

Industry observers note that founded in 2019, Villa says it has delivered more than 425 homes using an offsite construction model that spans accessory dwelling units (ADUs), multifamily projects and newly introduced neighborhoods. The firm manages feasibility, design, permitting, site preparation and installation, and partners with a network of factories for production, according to the announcement.

According to recent reports, messenger brings decades of financial and operating experience in homebuilding and multifamily real estate, having spent more than 10 years as chief financial officer of Century Communities. During his tenure, Century expanded from about 150 to 1,800 employees across 18 states, grew to $4.5 billion in annual revenue and more than 10,000 annual closings, completed seven acquisitions and raised more than $3 billion in debt and equity capital, the manufacturer noted.

Sources indicate that he also led Century’s initial public offering and helped launch its mortgage, title and insurance subsidiaries, giving him direct experience with the vertically integrated models many large homebuilders use to manage costs and capture more of the housing value chain. Earlier in his career, Messenger spent roughly a decade at UDR, a publicly traded multifamily real estate investment trust, where he advanced through senior finance roles to become CFO.

Messenger’s appointment comes as Villa looks to expand beyond individual ADUs and small projects into larger communities in partnership with land developers and homebuilders. The company is already working on latest neighborhoods including the 25-home Acacia Village in Santa Rosa, California, Alpine Village in Westminster, Colorado, and homes in Altadena, California, for families rebuilding after the Eaton Fire, according to the release.

Investors say his background in scaling a public homebuilder and in capital markets was a key factor in the decision.

Recent findings suggest that “Villa has demonstrated its capabilities across ADUs, multifamily properties and newly introduced neighborhoods, and Dave is the right leader to build on Villa’s success and advance its growth strategy,” said Aaron Marsh, partner and CFO at Unless, an investor in Villa and member of Villa’s board of directors. “He brings deep housing experience, a track record of scaling businesses nationally and a clear understanding of what land and development partners need to move projects forward.”.

Messenger stated he sees an opportunity to apply processes from large-scale homebuilding to Villa’s offsite platform.

In a recent development, “This team has done what much of our industry has only talked about: delivering quality homes through offsite construction across individual properties, multifamily communities and fresh neighborhoods,” Messenger remarked in the announcement. “I see great potential to build on that foundation by bringing a large-scale homebuilder’s operating discipline to Villa, with an emphasis on predictable execution and profitable growth.”.

Villa’s model aims to give homeowners, multifamily operators and developers a single partner from concept through completion. The tech giant handles site feasibility, site and home design, permitting and on-site work and uses factory partners to build homes offsite, aiming for more predictable timelines and costs than traditional stick-built construction, according to the release.

In a recent development, “Dave has an exceptional track record spanning homebuilding, multifamily real estate, capital markets and land development,” said Heather Miksch, chief operating officer at Villa. “As we build on Villa’s momentum and pursue development opportunities, his experience will be invaluable in helping us grow our business while continuing to serve both homeowners and development partners.”.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

AI-assisted summary, reviewed by NullTX editors.

AKT stakers are close to approving Akash's move from Cosmos to Solana, with Mintscan projecting a pass at 97.2% yes as voting enters its final hours.

But a yes on Proposal 346 opens a door rather than completing a move. Before a single AKT reaches Solana, two independent audits and at least two more on-chain votes still have to happen.

The summary going around is simple: Akash is leaving Cosmos for Solana. The proposal itself is narrower than that, and the details matter for anyone holding AKT.

Industry observers note that proposal 346 on akashnet-2, titled "Migrate the Akash Protocol to Solana," closes at 15:02 UTC on November 2. A yes vote approves the migration plan and authorises AKT to launch as an SPL token through a one-way portal that stays open for two years. It does not set a cutover date, it does not move a single lease, and on its own it does not open the portal.

The technical spec for that portal was published the day after voting opened. It shows how many further steps lie between this vote and a working SPL AKT.

The proposal text in Akash's AEP repository claims a yes vote does two things:.

It also claims plainly what it doesn't do: "it does not set a cutover date and does not move the marketplace." Live leases, staking and governance on akashnet-2 continue as normal. The marketplace moves only after audits and rehearsals pass and "a separate cutover proposal passes on this chain.".

Sources indicate that A no vote would stop the whole proposal. In the proposal's words: "Nothing moves; the token does not launch and the program returns to option analysis.".

At 08:43 UTC on November 2, about six hours before voting closed, Mintscan's page for Proposal 346 showed an expected result of "Will PASS":.

Turnout stood at 68.80% of bonded stake, against a quorum of 33.40%. The same figures can be read from Akash's own chain API, through the proposal object and its tally endpoint.

According to recent reports, mintscan's 97.2% is yes as a share of all votes cast. Akash's pass threshold leaves abstentions out, and on that basis yes stands at about 98.7%, far above the 50% needed. The veto share is negligible.

The tally has barely changed since early morning. A read of the chain at 07:29 UTC showed almost exactly the same totals, with only a handful of AKT added to the yes side. With turnout and margin that large, the outcome is not in doubt. The more useful question is what happens after it passes.

According to recent reports, the portal's design is in AEP-95, "One-Way AKT Sink to Solana,", a draft published on October 27 by core developers Artur Troian and Joseph Chalabi. It describes a "deliberately one-way" bridge with no return path. The authors say this removes "the largest class of bridge attacks.".

In a recent development, why supply doesn't change: every SPL AKT is backed by AKT locked on Akash, and nothing is minted independently on Solana. The token is a legacy SPL mint with six decimals and no freeze authority.

The spec's own risk table names the biggest trust point. The upgrade authority over the Solana programs could "mint without limit." That power is meant to sit with a time-locked multisig appointed by Akash governance, with monitors set to alert on every admin action.

At launch, SPL AKT has no protocol role. It will support "transfers and DEX liquidity only, with no staking or governance rights." Inflation stays on Akash. To seed trading, Overclock Labs, Akash's core developer, will send 1 million AKT through the bridge to a Solana treasury vault. That deposit follows the same rules as everyone else's.

Sources indicate that proposal 346 requires "two independent audits of the token and portal code before launch," with reports published within 30 days. AEP-95's launch sequence highlights what that requirement means on-chain.

Industry observers note that so Proposal 346 is the first of at least five on-chain decisions. The "2 to 3 weeks" launch estimate depends on the audits finishing and the upgrade and parameter votes passing on schedule.

For now, nothing. The proposal's disclosures set out what changes later:.

Discussion of the proposal continues in GitHub Discussion #1123.

The proposal lists four items as "still open, to be settled and published before the cutover proposal":.

The second item matters most to holders. The portal closes two years after launch, and the proposal doesn't yet say what happens to AKT that hasn't crossed by then. The final tally will confirm whether the initiative goes ahead, but that answer, and the decisions in the votes that follow, will matter more to most holders than today's margin.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Top performers report stronger AI returns, more reliable forecasts and better payback on developing their sellers.

PHILADELPHIA, Nov. 17, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Richardson Sales Performance, a global leader in sales training and performance improvement, today announced findings from a survey of 1,105 senior sales leaders at large global organizations. The study finds that while AI may have leveled the playing field, it has not leveled the results.

Top performers who met or exceeded quota report better results from AI, with 62% indicating a positive financial return vs. 39% of laggards. Additional findings:.

In a recent development, "Leaders at every performance level see the same market and share many of the same worries about AI," said Andrea Grodnitzky, chief marketing officer at Richardson Sales Performance. "What set top performers apart was what they did next. We conducted the research behind The Revenue Edge so sales leaders can see those practices clearly and compare them with their own.".

The Revenue Edge organizes these divergent approaches with others in forecasting, staffing and skill development into four distinct operating disciplines.

Underneath it all, leaders agree that selling stays human. Seventy percent say humans outperform AI on the activities that matter most in complex deals. Only 4% say AI does. Eighty-eight percent expect the skills AI can't replicate to set their best sellers apart in 2027.

Respondents were based in North America or Europe, hold a revenue leadership, general management or sales enablement leadership role at the vice president level or above, and worked at organizations with at least $750 million in annual revenue. Field dates were Oct. 12 to Oct. 20, 2026. Quota attainment is self-reported, so all comparisons are correlational. Top performers are leaders whose organizations met or exceeded quota (100% or more, n=497). Laggards are those below 90% of quota (n=338). Subgroup margins of error are about 4 points for top performers and about 5 points for laggards.

Download the full report at https://www.richardson.com/sales-resources/the-revenue-edge-research-report/.

Industry observers note that richardson is a global sales training and performance improvement company that helps organizations build confident sales teams and win more business in an increasingly complex buying environment. As buying groups expand, decision-making slows and AI reshapes how sales teams work, Richardson helps sellers combine consultative skills, disruptive insights and disciplined execution to move deals forward. Through proven methodologies, expert facilitation, customized learning, AI-enabled reinforcement and performance analytics, Richardson helps organizations develop the behaviors that improve customer conversations, strengthen pipeline progression and drive measurable revenue outcomes. The world's leading sales organizations rely on Richardson to build sales teams that compel buyers to act.

Media inquiries: Andrea Grodnitzky, [email protected].

#18464. What music sells a house? Agents say it’s not about genre

📅 13 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 8m • 📚 Deep Dive (1536 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Inman ↗ Open Full Page

What music sells a house? Agents say it’s not about genre

📅 13 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 8 min read (1536 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Inman

⏱️ ~8 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, taylor Swift, classical or silence?
  • In a recent development, ask real estate agents what soundtrack sells a house, and you’ll get two answers.
  • Inman asked agents and brokers from Manhattan to Breckenridge, Colorado, and they described the music they play at showings and open houses and how they match it to the property.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, taylor Swift, classical or silence? Agents explain how they pick open house music, the one rule most follow and why none can prove it works.

In a recent development, ask real estate agents what soundtrack sells a house, and you’ll get two answers. One is a carefully curated playlist, while the other is silence.

Inman asked agents and brokers from Manhattan to Breckenridge, Colorado, and they described the music they play at showings and open houses and how they match it to the property.

It has been revealed that none could point to hard numbers showing a playlist moved a home faster or for more money. What they did offer was a clear set of rules from the agents who use music, and an equally firm argument from those who won’t touch it.

Ben Jacobs, co-founder of the Chestler Jacobs Team at Douglas Elliman in New York City, thinks music raises more questions than it answers. He noted he’s not a fan of playing music during showings.

Industry observers note that “Buyers may wonder if the agent is trying to mask something, whether it’s street noise, construction nearby, sounds within the building or even a noisy appliance,” Jacobs told Inman. “You want buyers to experience the home as it actually is, without anything distracting from their ability to evaluate the space.”.

Industry observers note that his co-founder, Jessica Chestler, stated music has its place. That place is just not a private showing.

“Music can be wonderful for setting a mood at a cocktail party, listing launch or special event, but during a showing, I think there’s something to be said for letting the property speak for itself,” Chestler said.

Megan Sullivan works at the same brokerage, and she uses music for the very reason Jacobs avoids it. Sullivan sells large estate homes across Fairfield and Westchester counties out of Douglas Elliman’s Greenwich, Connecticut, office. Some of those homes sit within earshot of things a seller can’t fix.

“I actually do like incorporating music into certain showings, particularly when a property is impacted by outside noise from planes, trains or automobiles,” Sullivan mentioned. “Thoughtfully selected background music can help create a more welcoming atmosphere and soften those distractions, allowing buyers to focus on the overall experience of the home. I think it’s very property-specific.”.

In a recent development, jeffrey Hensel is a broker associate with North Coast Financial, a California hard money lender that funds fix-and-flip and probate deals. He looks at it from the investor side.

“Dead silence can amplify every creak, clank, and drip in an otherwise quiet home,” he said. “Background music masks these sounds and provides some white noise to help set a calm mood.”.

In a recent development, agents in the pro-music camp mostly aren’t trying to cover anything up. They simply want buyers to stay longer.

In a recent development, sandra Daniels of Harry Norman, Realtors | Forbes Global Properties serves the East Cobb and Marietta area outside Atlanta. She’s currently listing a $3.9 million estate in The River Club in Suwanee, Georgia.

For those showings, she rotates light classical piano, The Macarons Project and a Spotify playlist called “Nora Ephron + Nancy Meyers Dinner Party.”.

“Put a buyer in a home with a glass of Champagne or a cup of coffee and the right music playing, and that cozy, inviting atmosphere encourages people to stay, relax and feel at home,” Daniels told Inman.

It has been revealed that daniels also has a low-tech trick for vacant listings she expects to sell in the first week. She bought an old-school CD player and a few classical CDs. She leaves it on repeat through the first weekend of showings and stops by each evening to turn off the lights and music and lock up.

Natalia Bassova, founder and CEO of Resort Real Estate in Breckenridge, Colorado, saw the same effect at a luxury mountain listing. The home looked great, she stated, but it demonstrated cold.

Recent findings suggest that “By adding some background instrumental music, it gave the buyers more time to spend in the home. They spent more time in the kitchen and great room areas,” Bassova said. “The property didn’t change, but the atmosphere did.”.

For mountain and luxury homes, Bassova plays acoustic and piano music, including Ludovico Einaudi and The Piano Guys. For condos and new construction, she switches to soft contemporary instrumentals.

Agents who play music disagree on genre, but almost all agree on one thing: avoid lyrics.

Sources indicate that “If the buyer begins to think about the music, then it is having a negative impact,” Bassova remarked. Her never-play list covers anything with strong lyrics, politics, swearing or heavy bass.

Andrea Seeney is a global real estate advisor with Atlanta Fine Homes Sotheby’s International Realty and a trained opera singer and classical pianist. She compared lyrics to a seller’s personal effects.

“Acoustic performances are best because they set a tone and allow the buyer to fill in the blanks with their own thoughts,” Seeney said.

Recent findings suggest that she leans toward jazz and usually plays Spotify’s Coffee House radio or its Ella Fitzgerald playlist. She indicates music works on buyers through memory: a song can take someone back to a time and place they enjoyed, “and that memory then reflects positively on the home.”.

Hensel takes the lyrics rule a step further, to genre itself. If an agent plays hip-hop or country for a buyer who doesn’t listen to it, he notes, that signals an assumption about who the buyer is. That can create friction neither side notices. His pick is quiet cocktail-lounge jazz like Miles Davis or Bill Evans, at a steady tempo and volume.

Recent findings suggest that he also cited retail research by psychological scientists Adrian North and Lorraine Sheridan of Curtin University and Charles Areni of Macquarie University. It found that shoppers who heard classical music rated merchandise as higher quality and were willing to spend more.

Some agents ignore the rulebook completely.

Industry observers note that rachel Kilmer, an agent with ReeceNichols Real Estate in Kansas City, Missouri, plays Taylor Swift at nearly every open house. She swaps in country for more rural listings.

Recent findings suggest that “In Kansas City, she’s a conversation starter,” Kilmer stated. “People come in, and it’s, ‘Are you a Swiftie?’ ‘No, but I love the Chiefs!’ It really helps loosen up the conversation.”.

She added, “I’m the one sitting there listening to it for two hours!”.

Monica Shea, a broker with KW Aspire in Colorado Springs, Colorado, builds whole open houses around a theme, and the music follows.

She played the Eras Tour set list at a Taylor Swift–themed open house and the Frozen soundtrack at a hot cocoa bar event. A Halloween open house got not-too-spooky Halloween music. For regular showings, she has sellers put on a YouTube channel with seasonal background music and scenery.

Sources indicate that shea’s never-play list puts her directly at odds with a few other agents: smooth jazz. Shea states she never plays “anything that sounds like the Weather Channel.”.

Sources indicate that marcel Finkelstein of Team BlackStar at eXp Realty hosts open houses every Sunday across Monmouth County, Newly introduced Jersey. He sees music as more of an icebreaker than a staging tool.

According to recent reports, his Apple Music rotation includes lounge instrumentals, vocal-free dance-pop and Bon Entendeur. It also has Afro house from DJ Alex Niyazov and the warm trumpet and sax of Fausto Papetti and Paul Mauriat.

He uses the same approach whether the listing is a $600,000 two-bedroom condo in Manalapan or a $2 million six-bedroom in Colts Neck.

“I want the atmosphere to feel calm, comfortable and welcoming, rather than like a sales presentation,” Finkelstein said.

Finkelstein added that his Instagram followers also know how much he loves music.

It has been revealed that “Every week, I share new songs and incorporate music into my stories and posts about homes,” he mentioned. “It’s a personal interest that carries through into how I present properties.”.

Recent findings suggest that on setup, agents who play music give similar advice. Keep the volume low enough that buyers can ask questions and the agent can hear their feedback. Use one good speaker rather than several.

Bassova puts hers in the middle of the home, and Seeney puts a small Bluetooth speaker in the kitchen. When sellers have a Sonos system, Daniels connects to it from her MacBook or iPad. Otherwise, she brings her own Bose speaker.

According to recent reports, kilmer runs her music from an iPad instead of her phone. “That way, incoming calls and texts don’t interrupt the music,” she mentioned.

As for proof, none of the agents Inman spoke with track music as a performance metric. Bassova said she gets buyer feedback that certain homes feel relaxing, but nothing tied to days on market or offers.

So the evidence is anecdotal, and the playlists don’t agree. Agents can’t even settle on jazz. Both camps share one goal: the buyer should notice the home, not the soundtrack.

As Bassova said, “If the buyer begins to think about the music, then it is having a negative impact.”.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that black Rifle Coffee looks to shut 12 shops that it operates itself as part of Project Core, a restructuring program, parent company BRC stated as it reported third-quarter results on Nov. 2. The company calls the shops Outposts.

Recent findings suggest that BRC reported a net loss of $8.7 million for the quarter, compared with $1.2 million in the third quarter of 2025. Net revenue rose 7.3% to $108.0 million, driven by wholesale and direct-to-consumer sales. Wholesale revenue grew to $72.5 million, an 8.1% gain, while direct-to-consumer revenue reached $30.2 million, up 8.5%.

Industry observers note that outpost revenue came in at $5.4 million, down 8.0% from $5.8 million in the third quarter of 2025. The company stated the drop stemmed from weaker sales at the Outposts it runs itself, while franchise and non-traditional locations grew and recouped some of the loss. As of Sept. 30, Black Rifle had 17 company-owned and 22 franchise Outposts.

"These actions mark a significant step toward a more asset-light operating model, which we expect will support franchise-led retail growth, lower capital requirements, and create a more efficient cost structure," Chief Financial Officer Matt Amigh said in a statement.

The company also modified eight leases on sites where development aims have been shelved, and it closed the divestiture of a direct-to-consumer brand outside its core business. It signed a definitive agreement under which a manufacturing partner will buy its roasting facility in Manchester, Tennessee, Amigh noted.

Chief Executive Officer Chris Mondzelewski described Project Core as a multi-year initiative to sharpen the focus on the core coffee business and brand, improve profitability, simplify operations and reduce capital intensity.

According to recent reports, other operating expenses rose to $9.3 million in the quarter from $0.6 million in the third quarter of 2025. The manufacturer attributed the increase to impairments at some Outposts under Project Core and to a reserve set aside for a legal contingency, partly offset by gains on lease terminations and the brand sale. Adjusted EBITDA, a non-GAAP measure, rose 12.3% to $9.5 million.

Black Rifle reaffirmed its full-year 2026 outlook, which calls for revenue to grow by 8% or more and adjusted EBITDA to grow by 35% or more. The outlook includes an expected fourth-quarter revenue headwind of about $3 million from the brand sale and the planned Outpost closures, the manufacturer said.

Black Rifle has not published a full roster of which shops will shut down, according to Men's Journal.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Corma.ai Ltd., a startup that develops artificial intelligence models for cybersecurity teams, has raised $125 million in funding.
  • In a recent development, NEA led the Series A round.
  • Recent findings suggest that corma, which has offices in San Francisco and Tel Aviv, indicates competing AI models are often better at launching cyberattacks than fixing them.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

UPDATED 18:48 EST / NOVEMBER 16 2026.

Corma.ai Ltd., a startup that develops artificial intelligence models for cybersecurity teams, has raised $125 million in funding.

In a recent development, NEA led the Series A round. Corma stated today that returning backers Khosla Ventures, Coatue and Sequoia Capital chipped in as well. The tech giant is now valued at $1 billion.

Recent findings suggest that corma, which has offices in San Francisco and Tel Aviv, indicates competing AI models are often better at launching cyberattacks than fixing them. The organization recently conducted a test in which it asked several large language models to hack a simulated corporate network. They succeeded at installing a malicious file across 85% of the test runs. In contrast, the models found only 12% of the malicious files that they themselves installed.

It has been revealed that according to Corma, the gap between LLMs’ offensive and defensive capabilities can give hackers an edge over cybersecurity teams. That’s the problem the company is tackling with its cybersecurity-optimized AI models. Corma says that the algorithms can speed up some breach response workflows by a factor of 100 while reducing the associated costs.

According to recent reports, the manufacturer benchmarked one of its models against the competition using an evaluation called DefenseBench V5. The test measures two metrics: how reliably a model performs defensive cybersecurity tasks and how fast it completes them. Corma says that its model outperformed GPT-6 Astra, Claude Opus 5.5 and several other cutting-edge LLMs.

According to recent reports, the firm’s algorithms find breaches by analyzing data from other cybersecurity tools. Corma can ingest telemetry generated by firewalls, network monitoring software and a range of other applications. The company says that its models not only find threats but also generate remediation guidance for each one.

According to recent reports, automating breach response tasks is difficult because it requires LLMs to filter numerous false positives and duplicate alerts. Moreover, models often have access to only partial information about breaches. Many companies discard cybersecurity logs after a relatively short amount of time to reduce data storage costs.

According to recent reports, corma says that its algorithms can perform breach investigations on a fully autonomous basis. If human input is needed, they alert a relevant member of the cybersecurity team. It’s also possible to manually steer Corma’s models via a Slack chatbot. An administrator could, for example, ask Corma to double-check whether a recent effort to remove malware from a compromised server was successful.

“Since we came out of stealth, demand from the world’s largest organizations has been overwhelming, and one of our hardest problems has been securing capacity fast enough to keep up with the demand,” stated Corma co-founder and Chief Executive Officer Alon Pluda.

Corma will use its newly raised funds to buy more infrastructure and enhance its AI models.

Hedge fund pressures Invitation Homes to speed up home sales

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Activist investor Land & Buildings Investment Management is pressing single-family rental giant Invitation Homes to accelerate home sales, sharply increase capital returns and scale back growth aims, arguing the company’s stock trades at a steep discount to the value of its houses.
  • In an open letter to shareholders released Monday, the Stamford, Connecticut-based hedge fund noted it believes Invitation Homes is “among the most undervalued companies in the REIT sector” and criticized the board and management for what it called “complacency” and “half measures” in addressing the gap.
  • Recent findings suggest that land & Buildings, which owns an undisclosed stake in Invitation Homes, is led by Jonathan Litt, a longtime activist in the real estate investment trust sector.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Activist investor Land & Buildings Investment Management is pressing single-family rental giant Invitation Homes to accelerate home sales, sharply increase capital returns and scale back growth aims, arguing the company’s stock trades at a steep discount to the value of its houses.

In an open letter to shareholders released Monday, the Stamford, Connecticut-based hedge fund noted it believes Invitation Homes is “among the most undervalued companies in the REIT sector” and criticized the board and management for what it called “complacency” and “half measures” in addressing the gap.

Recent findings suggest that land & Buildings, which owns an undisclosed stake in Invitation Homes, is led by Jonathan Litt, a longtime activist in the real estate investment trust sector. Invitation Homes (NYSE: INVH) is the nation’s largest owner of single-family rental homes, with more than 80,000 properties concentrated in Sun Belt and other high-growth markets.

Industry observers note that land & Buildings said the public market values Invitation Homes’ properties at roughly $270,000 per home, compared with an average sale price of about $460,000 on homes the company has sold since December 2025. That implies a discount of about 40%, according to the letter, which was disseminated via GlobeNewswire.

Industry observers note that the firm remarked it separately valued more than 90% of the organization’s wholly owned portfolio, “address by address,” and arrived at an estimated average value of approximately $425,000 per home. That analysis underpins its net asset value estimate of about $45 per share, which Land & Buildings said is more than 65% above Invitation Homes’ current trading price even after assuming 6% selling costs on every home.

“REITs with sound fundamentals and no distressed assets do not trade at such a discount indefinitely. Something has to give,” the firm remarked in the letter.

Recent findings suggest that “Invitation Homes’ Board of Directors and management team are committed to acting in the best interests of the Company and its shareholders to deliver long-term, sustainable value,” says a prepared statement from the company. “Our focus is on strengthening our foundation and enhancing the resident experience that sets us apart. This focus has resulted in solid operational and financial performance in recent quarters, supported by consistent demand, strong retention, and continued execution across our core markets.”.

Industry observers note that “We are always open to hearing and considering the perspectives of our shareholders. Members of our Board and management team have had numerous discussions with Land & Buildings over the past several months to better understand its views, as we would with any shareholder. While we are disappointed that Land & Buildings has chosen to make its issues public at this time, we remain open to further engagement.”.

In a recent development, land & Buildings has highlighted what it described as sustained underperformance. Over the trailing one-, three- and five-year periods, Invitation Homes has lagged the S&P 500, the broader REIT index, its closest peer American Homes 4 Rent and the proxy peer group the board uses for benchmarking executive compensation, the letter remarked.

It has been revealed that over the past three years, Invitation Homes ranks second to last in that compensation peer group, trailing the group average by more than 35 percentage points, according to Land & Buildings. Shareholders who held the stock for five years have lost more than 20% of their investment, including dividends, the letter noted, even as U.S. home prices have continued to climb.

In a recent development, the firm noted that Invitation Homes’ shares now trade at an implied capitalization rate of about 7%, roughly 60 basis points wider than American Homes 4 Rent, and at a lower multiple of adjusted funds from operations. The stock trades only modestly above its $20 IPO price from early 2017 while national home prices are up nearly 80% over that period, according to the letter.

Land & Buildings blamed Invitation Homes’ strategy for much of the gap. The company was a net buyer of homes in every year from 2022 through 2025 despite “a poor cost of capital,” and earnings have “repeatedly fallen short of expectations,” the firm noted.

The letter also pointed to legal and regulatory costs. Land & Buildings noted Invitation Homes has paid more than $79 million to resolve four legal matters related to resident treatment and business practices, including a $48 million settlement with the Federal Trade Commission in 2024. At the same time, the board approved more than $25 million in special retention awards in March 2026 for the CEO and three other executives, according to the firm.

“This troubling misalignment and lack of accountability is deeply concerning,” Land & Buildings stated.

The activist laid out a three-part plan it says could unlock value and narrow the discount to net asset value:.

Land & Buildings estimated that a multi-year, programmatic asset sale and capital return program could deliver “substantial annual accretion” to both earnings and NAV per share, supported by what it pegged as nearly $40 billion of gross asset value.

The letter criticized what Land & Buildings characterized as incremental steps by Invitation Homes, including recent home sales and share repurchases, arguing those moves have not been sized or communicated in a way that would change how investors value the company.

“Half measures appear to be this Board’s modus operandi: do just enough to relieve pressure while preserving the status quo,” the firm wrote.

In a recent development, land & Buildings also objected to the board’s Nov. 11 appointment of Colin Connolly, CEO of office REIT Cousins Properties, as a fresh director. The firm said the board had previously told it that refreshment was not needed and argued that adding another sitting REIT chief executive provided “duplicative skill sets” rather than shareholder alignment and capital allocation expertise.

The activist said independent research firm Green Street wrote less than a year ago that Invitation Homes should “shrink its portfolio, return capital to shareholders, and redirect the bulk of its energy internally on operations until its valuation improves.” Land & Buildings said it had urged management to outline a clear, multi-year capital return blueprint at REIT conferences in September but came away with “little more than lip service.”.

Invitation Homes did not immediately respond to a request for comment on the letter or the firm’s proposals. The company has previously defended its strategy of balancing internal growth, acquisitions and select dispositions as it manages a large, geographically diverse portfolio in a tight housing market.

Industry observers note that the campaign underscores how corporate decisions at large institutional single-family landlords can influence for-sale and rental supply in already constrained markets. Land & Buildings’ proposal would require Invitation Homes to sell thousands of homes a year to owner-occupiers or directly to existing tenants at retail pricing.

Recent findings suggest that for homebuilders and real estate agents, a large program of individual home sales by Invitation Homes could add incremental existing-home inventory in high-demand metros where resale listings remain scarce. The suggested 6% down-payment rebate for tenants could create a new pipeline of first-time buyers but might also draw scrutiny from policymakers and tenant advocates who have criticized investor ownership of single-family homes.

According to recent reports, for other single-family rental REITs and institutional owners, the dispute highlights growing pressure from investors to prioritize buybacks and capital returns over portfolio growth when shares trade at discounts to estimated property values. If Invitation Homes embraced or was forced into a multi-year shrink-to-grow strategy, it could reset expectations for capital allocation across the sector.

Land & Buildings mentioned it prefers to work “constructively” with Invitation Homes but “will not hesitate to take whatever steps we believe are necessary to maximize value,” a signal that a proxy fight or board challenge is on the table heading into the 2027 proxy season.

Ackman states Trump can still end GSE conservatorships, relist this term

📅 16 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (521 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Housingwire

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Bill Ackman still believes Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac can be relisted on the Upcoming York Stock Exchange and exit their conservatorships before the end of President Donald Trump’s second term, even after Democrats won control of both chambers in the midterm elections.
  • In a letter to Pershing Square Holdings shareholders signed in early November, Ackman, the company’s founder and CEO, and chief investment officer Ryan Israel wrote that “a relisting and release from conservatorship can be accomplished by the President using his executive authority without any involvement of Congress.”.
